Laptop Log Collector  v2.1
======================================================================

1. What this is
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A one-click log collection tool for laptop testers. Tick the items you need;
the tool copies the logs, system information, crash dumps, power and
performance data into one folder and generates an HTML report that can be
handed straight to engineering.

No installation, no network access, no changes to system settings.
The interface and all generated reports are in English.

2. Requirements
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit), any display language
- Portable: a single exe, no .NET / Python / runtime required
- Run as administrator recommended (otherwise dumps, WER and the sleep study
  report are skipped)

3. Three steps
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Double-click LogCollector.exe
2) Type the name of the collector in "Collected by" at the top
3) Tick what to collect (the common set is already ticked)
4) Optionally change the output folder: type a path, or press "Browse..."
   to pick one (the default is Desktop\LogCollection)
5) Click "Start collection" and wait for the progress bar

An "Open the HTML report now?" prompt appears when done.

Avoid using the machine while collecting.

4. What each item collects
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The number in front of each item is the output folder number: item 4 writes
to 4_System_Info, item 16 to 16_Battery, and so on.

[Basics]
  1  System event log                  System.evtx plus the full event list as CSV
  2  Application event log             Application.evtx plus the full event list as CSV
  3  All event log files (.evtx)       every .evtx under winevt\Logs, folder
                                       structure mirrored incl. empty folders
  4  System info (systeminfo)          full systeminfo report
  5  Driver store and problem devices  driver store listing + devices with a
                                       yellow mark in Device Manager
  6  Running processes                 every process running at collection time
  7  Installed updates and software    updates and installed programs
  8  msinfo32 full report (slow)       more detail, may hang (off by default)

[Crashes and dumps]
  9  Blue screen dumps (Minidump)      copies every .dmp in the Minidump folder
 10  WER crash reports (full folder)   mirrors C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER
                                       with its structure; needs admin
 11  Live kernel reports               mirrors C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports
                                       (GPU hangs/timeouts without a BSOD); needs admin
 12  Full memory dump (MEMORY.DMP)     only if the system already created it

[Setup and component logs]
 13  Windows setup logs (Panther)      mirrors C:\Windows\Panther: setupact.log,
                                       setupapi, migration and rollback data
                                       (can be ~2 GB; needs admin)
 14  Windows component logs            mirrors C:\Windows\Logs: CBS, DISM,
                                       WindowsUpdate, WinRE, MoSetup
 15  Driver INF and setup logs         mirrors C:\Windows\INF incl. setupapi.dev.log

[Power and battery]
 16  Battery health report             design/full capacity, cycles, drain curve
 17  Power settings                    sleep/hibernate/display/disk timeouts,
                                       lid and power button action, hybrid sleep
 18  Sleep study + system power report powercfg /sleepstudy and powercfg /spr
                                       (sleepstudy-report.html); needs admin

[Performance]
 19  DXDiag (graphics and display)     dxdiag report: GPU driver, display modes

[Network]
 20  Network configuration snapshot    IP, routes, DNS, Wi-Fi, proxy, TCP

[Storage]
 21  Disk and SMART health             health, temperature, power-on hours, wear

5. Output
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Default output folder: Desktop\LogCollection\
Each run creates a folder named <BIOS serial>_<timestamp>, for example
N4N0CV01760013H_20261107-162543. The serial number is read from the BIOS
(Win32_BIOS.SerialNumber). If the BIOS returns a placeholder such as
"Default string", the model name is used instead and the log says so.
The timestamp keeps several runs on the same machine apart.

The folder contains:

  report.html            start here: key findings, event timeline,
                         hardware, battery and power settings
  All_Content.html       every text file in one browsable page
  Collection_Info.txt    what was collected, status and how to read it
  Collected_By.txt       who collected this package and when

  1_System_Logs\         System.evtx
                         System_events.csv    every event, full messages (30 days)
                         System_errors.csv    errors + warnings only (AI friendly)
  2_Application_Logs\    Application.evtx + Application_events.csv
                         + Application_errors.csv
  3_All_Event_Logs\      all .evtx files: Logs\ is an exact mirror of winevt\Logs
                         (empty folders included) when run as administrator;
                         otherwise Channels\ holds one .evtx per exported channel
  4_System_Info\         systeminfo.txt
  5_Drivers_Devices\     driver_store.txt / problem_devices.txt
  6_Runtime_Snapshot\    running_processes.txt
  7_Installed_Updates_and_Software\
                         installed_updates_and_software.txt
  8_msinfo32\            msinfo32.txt
  9_Crash_Dumps\         blue screen dmp files
 10_WER_Reports\         WER\ mirrors C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER
 11_LiveKernel_Reports\  mirrors C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports
 12_Memory_Dump\         MEMORY.DMP
 13_Setup_Panther\       Panther\ mirrors C:\Windows\Panther
 14_Windows_Logs\        Logs\ mirrors C:\Windows\Logs
 15_Inf_Drivers\         INF\ mirrors C:\Windows\INF
 16_Battery\             battery_report.html
 17_Power_Settings\      power_settings.txt
 18_Sleep_Study\ 19_DXDiag\ 20_Network\ 21_Storage\

Only the folders for the items you ticked are created.

Folders whose copy was incomplete contain Skipped_Files.txt listing what was
left out (for example files that were locked or did not fit the free space).

"Status: Skipped" means there was nothing to collect (for example no BSOD
has occurred). The reason is written to README.txt inside that folder.

6. Memory dumps
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Blue screen dumps are written by Windows, not by this tool. Whether you get
a GB-sized file depends on the setting "Write debugging information":

  Small memory dump    ~256 KB per crash, MEMORY.DMP is never created
  Kernel memory dump   MEMORY.DMP, usually 1-4 GB      <- usually enough
  Complete memory dump MEMORY.DMP, about the size of RAM

To change it: This PC > Properties > Advanced system settings > Startup and
Recovery > Settings > "Write debugging information". A reboot is required,
and the file only appears after the next BSOD. The page file must also be
large enough (system managed, or >= 16 GB), otherwise writing the dump fails.

7. FAQ
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Q: The header says "Standard user: some items unavailable".
A: Click "Restart as administrator", or right-click the exe and choose
   "Run as administrator". Most items still work without admin.

Q: An item shows "Skipped" - is the tool broken?
A: No. Skipped means there was nothing to collect, for example no BSOD has
   occurred so there is no dump. The reason is in that folder's README.txt
   and also listed in the report.

Q: No dump collected for a BSOD
A: Check the dump setting printed in 9_Crash_Dumps\README.txt. Most often
   the system is set to "Small memory dump" or no BSOD has occurred yet.

Q: How long does a collection take?
A: About 1.5 minutes with the default items; add a minute or two if you tick
   the setup logs (Panther can be ~2 GB).

Q: What are the actual sleep / hibernate timeouts?
A: See 17_Power_Settings\power_settings.txt or the "Power and sleep settings"
   table in the report. AC (plugged in) and DC (battery) are listed
   separately. "Never" means it does not trigger automatically.

Q: Where does the collector name go?
A: Into Collected_By.txt in the package root, and into Collection_Info.txt
   and the report header.

Q: Why is there no SOURCE.txt or browse.html any more?
A: They were removed to keep the package small. Where each file came from is
   recorded in Collection_Info.txt and the report, and all text content is in
   the single All_Content.html.

8. Command line
----------------------------------------------------------------------
LogCollector.exe /cli /out:D:\logs /jobs:events-system,sysinfo,minidump
LogCollector.exe /cli /all /out:D:\logs /tag:SN1234567
LogCollector.exe /cli /out:D:\logs /jobs:disk /case:12345

Options: /cli no UI, /out output folder, /jobs comma separated item ids,
/all every item, /tag package name prefix, /case case id,
/symptom symptom text.

9. Notes
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- The tool only reads data. It does not clear logs, change settings or
  install anything.
- Reports and logs may contain personal data (user names, paths, SSIDs).
  Handle them according to your data classification policy.
- The .evtx mirror and the Panther folder can be large; watch the free disk
  space.
